nodes.description: The milder classes. In the same cohort these are groups 3 to 5: alleles leading to haploinsufficiency, non-glycine missense alleles within the triple helix, and non-glycine missense or in-frame insertion-deletion alleles in the N- or C-terminal part of the protein. Patients in those three groups had a less typical phenotype and no digestive events. The record is named for the two classes the authors single out in their conclusion, haploinsufficiency and the terminal non-glycine alleles.

nodes.description: COL3A1 variants disrupt type III collagen triple-helix formation, secretion, and extracellular-matrix deposition. Glycine substitutions destroy the triple-helical winding, so misfolded procollagen III is retained in the endoplasmic reticulum and secretion of functionally mature collagen III is impaired. The resulting collagen III matrix weakness compromises blood-vessel and hollow-organ tensile strength, leading to arterial dissection or rupture, intestinal perforation, uterine rupture, easy bruising, and thin translucent skin.
